subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must decide whether coordinate points lie on one straight line
use after ordered-pair and slope semantics are stable
anchor: Three points are collinear when the direction from one point to each of the others is the same; equal defined slopes are one algebraic test of that common direction.
ordinary_language_bridge: Same straight line means same direction, not merely same plane or same x/y coordinate.
reconstruction_route: conclude only after the direction test

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: three points in the coordinate plane
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: all points share a plane versus all points share one line
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: What extra condition beyond being in the plane is required?

misconception_discriminator.probe: show three visibly non-collinear planar points and ask whether coplanarity is sufficient
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner rejects coplanarity and invokes one-line/common-direction condition

repair_route: use common reference point and two slopes
include a vertical-line example to prevent formula-only dependence
verification_method: compare two slopes from the same reference point or verify a common line equation
handle vertical direction explicitly rather than divide by zero
known_limitations: slope comparison needs a vertical-line branch
does not teach the full theory of affine dependence
